items.item_text: Current California RN license.
OCN certification.
BART or BLS at time of hire with commitment to get BART within six (6) months of hire date.
ONS Chemotherapy and Biotherapy certification with recent experience (within the last 6 months).
Must be able to work various hours and locations based on business needs.
Employment is subject to a criminal background check and pre-employment physical.
Must be able to work at least 3 weekend days a month.
Minimum one (1) year of recent (within the last 6 months) oncology infusion center or acute care oncology experience.
Recent infusion center experience.
Experience actively administering a wide variety of chemotherapy regimens and corresponding knowledge of oncology diagnoses and treatments.
Clinical Trials Infusion experience.

UC San Diego Health is proud to be a four-time Magnet-designated organization and has now earned Magnet with Distinction from the American Nurses Credentialing Center (ANCC). Magnet is the gold standard for nursing excellence, achieved by only about 10% of hospitals worldwide. Magnet with Distinction is awarded to the highest-performing Magnet organizations, with only a select few earning this prestigious honor. This recognition reflects our commitment to transformational leadership, professional nursing excellence, innovation, exceptional patient outcomes, and an empowering practice environment where nurses thrive.

This Infusion RN position requires excellent written/verbal communication and critical thinking skills in the delivery of oncology and non-oncology infusion therapy and related services (clinical trials, labs, dressing changes, injections, and so forth). The Infusion RN gives chemotherapy, biotherapy, clinical trials infusion, and other infusion-related services as well as blood work, dressing changes, and injections in a fast-paced outpatient infusion center setting. This position will receive training in clinical trials.

Using the nursing process, the Infusion RN ensures patient safety, symptom management, and patient/family education in a fast-paced outpatient infusion center. The Infusion RN must proactively anticipate and respond to urgent medical emergencies. Commitment to teamwork and engagement are also vital to this role to sustain our commitment to a healthy work environment.

Autonomous nursing care is the ability of a nurse to assess and provide nursing actions as appropriate for patient care populations based on competence, professional expertise, and knowledge. The nurse is expected to practice autonomously consistent with ANA Standards of Practice and Professional Performance. Independent judgment is expected to be exercised within the context of interdisciplinary and multidisciplinary approaches to patient care.
While not required, a cover letter is highly recommended when applying to this position.
Must be a graduate of an accredited school of Nursing.
BSN.
Must complete CTI Training within 6 months of hire.
Consistently demonstrates empathy and kindness while communicating and collaborating effectively with staff at all levels, physicians, patients, and external partners.

Demonstrates strong independent judgment and critical-thinking skills, with the ability to make sound decisions, solve problems efficiently, and prioritize multiple layers of information and responsibilities to quickly assess moderately complex situations and develop effective solutions.
Demonstrates the ability to work effectively in a fast-paced clinical environment while utilizing strong interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills.
